summary.headline: Vishnu Chemicals Q2 FY27 revenue rose 7.1% YoY to ₹429.5 crore and EBITDA 10% to ₹64 crore, with margin at 14.9%, while logistics costs squeezed exports.
summary.overview: Consolidated operating revenue grew 7.1% YoY to ₹429.53 crore and PAT rose 8.2% to ₹35.57 crore in Q2 FY27, with EBITDA margin at 14.9%. H1 FY27 revenue grew 15.4% to ₹862.3 crore and PAT grew 15.5% to ₹75.21 crore. Export volumes, mainly base chrome cargo to the US and Europe, were hit by freight costs, which management says rose to 8.8% of operating revenue from 5.9% in Q1; domestic share rose to 58%. Management guided to an EBITDA margin recovery toward 17-18% and a target of about 20% consolidated, with new products (DMSO, chrome metal JV) and a credit rating upgrade to A (stable) from ICRA.

financial_highlights.metric: Logistics cost as % of export sales

segments.name: Chrome chemicals
segments.commentary: Management says chromic acid, sodium dichromate and barium chemicals were not impacted by freight; base chrome cargo for leather to the US and Europe saw volume drop, with a value loss of about ₹25-30 crore a quarter. Chrome capacity utilisation is above 75%.

segments.name: Barium chemicals
segments.commentary: Utilisation is about 70%, with no further capex planned; management says the business is cash generative after completing backward and forward integration. EBITDA margin expected to be sustained if markets are stable.

segments.name: Strontium chemicals
segments.commentary: Capacity of about 12,000 tpa; management targets 70% utilisation in the second year of operations. Revenue was similar to Q1 at about ₹25 crore, and customer approvals are coming in India. No EBITDA margin guidance was given.

segments.name: DMSO (new)
segments.commentary: Plant of 10,000 tpa expected to start around Q4 FY27 with 50-60% utilisation in year one and margins similar to barium (about 25%). Capex about ₹250 crore.

guidance_outlook: Export volumes expected to recover by Q4 FY27 as freight normalises; management says Q3 should improve on Q2.
EBITDA margin expected to recover toward 17-18% in the year ahead, with a 20% consolidated target if DMSO, oxide and Europe shipments come through.
Management targets about 18-19% EBITDA margin for FY28 in one answer, and later about 20% consolidated.
Capex of about ₹524 crore in total; about ₹190 crore spent so far and about ₹300-330 crore to be spent over the next 12 months, funded partly by debt, with peak debt of ₹800-820 crore.
South Africa mine processing plant commissioning targeted; shipments to India expected from Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: Chrome metal JV with DCX Chrome France: 6,000 tpa high-purity chrome metal greenfield plant at Visakhapatnam; first phase targeted for next financial year; upwards of 20% EBITDA margin expected.
DMSO plant: 10,000 tpa, expected to start around Q4 FY27; capex about ₹250 crore.

Chrome oxide green (about 20,000 tpa incremental) and chromic acid (about 5-6,000 tpa incremental) expansion; capex about ₹220 crore. Sodium dichromate expansion completed, taking capacity to 90,000 tpa.
Strontium capacity 12,000 tpa already set up; utilisation target 70% in second year.

Solar capacity addition of about 20 MW, taking solar generation to nearly 6x current levels. Visakhapatnam plant had a temporary shutdown from 20 October for maintenance and capex tie-ins, restart planned shortly after the call.
demand_pricing: Export freight cost was 20-25% of selling price on base chrome cargo; management expects customers to re-contract over 5-6 month cycles, so volume recovery is seen in Q4.
Chrome metal: India imports about 1,700-1,800 tpa, growing about 12-13%; demand about 2,000 tpa; 60-70% of planned output to be exported. Global chrome metal index about $10.1-10.5/kg.
Chromic acid: 60-70% domestic market share; oxide has a firm purchase order from a European partner.
Receivable days rose to about 72-73 days at 30 Sep 2026 from 62 days a year earlier; inventory days rose due to freight and geopolitical uncertainty.
Management sees raw material (sulfuric acid, sulfur) and energy costs as the main source of volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Have exports been lost to supply chain disruption, and how much value was lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight hit base chrome cargo to the US and Europe, with value loss of about ₹25-30 crore a quarter; value-added products were not affected. Recovery is expected in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA outlook for the strontium business?
qa_highlights.answer: No margin guidance given; revenue was similar to Q1 and customer approvals are coming in India. Utilisation target is 70% next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the temporary Visakhapatnam plant shutdown?
qa_highlights.answer: No business loss expected, as adequate starting and value-added product inventory is held; the shutdown allowed maintenance and capex tie-ins after cyclones.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹524 crore total, of which ₹190 crore is spent; about ₹300-330 crore remains. Peak debt is expected at ₹800-820 crore, with the rest funded internally.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for South African mine shipments?
qa_highlights.answer: Mining has started; the processing plant is in commissioning, with shipments to India expected from Q4 FY27 and a significant contribution in FY28.

risks_watch: Freight and logistics costs remain elevated (Q2 logistics 8.8% of revenue vs 5.9% in Q1); recovery depends on Q3-Q4 normalisation.
Receivable and inventory days rising to about 72-73 days, which ties up working capital.
Chrome and strontium margins have been volatile; management gave no margin guidance for strontium.
Execution risk on DMSO ramp-up (50-60% utilisation in year one), the chrome metal JV (FY28 start) and the South African mine processing plant.
Consolidated EBITDA margin target of 17-20% depends on several new product ramps and freight easing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term margins and new products, but cautious on near-term freight and logistics, with management repeatedly saying targets are "cautiously optimistic". Several answers on timelines and margins were qualitative, with no numbers given for strontium EBITDA or DMSO margin beyond about 25%.
key_quotes: We have been able to sustain our operating margins despite continued pressure from elevated logistics cost and uncertainty in the end user market.
We are also pleased to share an important strategic development in our chromium business.
So we are expecting the volumes for this particular business to come back in quarter four.
